ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the isobar distribution map of a certain region of the world at a certain moment in a certain month. <image1> At this time, what is the wind direction in the city of Viedma (64°W, 40°30′S)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows an isobar map of southern South America and its nearby sea areas, with the 40°S and 50°S latitude lines and about 74°W and 66°W longitude lines marked. The coordinates of Viedma are 64°W, 40°30′S, so its position should be in eastern Argentina in the diagram, in the eastern area close to and south of the 40°S latitude line. The nearby isobars there are roughly distributed in a northwest—southeast direction, with relatively higher pressure nearby to the north and relatively lower pressure to the south or southwest. According to the isobars, the horizontal pressure gradient force points from high pressure toward low pressure; this region is located in the Southern Hemisphere, so under the action of the geostrophic deflection force, the wind is deflected to the left relative to the pressure-gradient direction, and under the influence of near-surface friction it slightly crosses the isobars and flows toward the low-pressure side. Therefore, the actual wind direction near Viedma generally appears as air flowing from the north toward the south nearby, namely wind blowing from the north.

raw_record.question_text:
Read the isobar distribution map of a certain region of the world at a certain moment in a certain month.

<image1>

At this time, what is the wind direction in the city of Viedma (64°W, 40°30′S)?

method.method_draft: Locate 64°W, 40°30′S on the isobar map, determine the local pressure-gradient direction from the labeled/neighboring isobars, then rotate the high-to-low flow leftward for the Southern Hemisphere and allow for a small cross-isobar component toward low pressure. The resulting air movement is generally from north toward south near Biedma, so report the wind as coming from the north: 偏北风.
